sub: A centrifugal concentrator spins slurry in a bowl to separate free gold from lighter material. Screened feed and clean water help the unit work effectively.
A modular gold plant combines processing stages in units that can be transported and connected on site. Its layout needs to suit your ore tests and site conditions.
A ball mill uses tumbling steel balls to grind crushed ore and release gold from the surrounding rock. The required grind and ore hardness guide the choice of mill.
A jaw crusher compresses rock between fixed and moving plates to reduce its size. This prepares the material for the next crushing or grinding stage in your plant.
A cone crusher reduces rock after primary crushing to prepare finer feed for milling. Its discharge setting needs to suit the next processing stage in your plant.
A hammer mill uses swinging hammers to break ore by impact. A discharge screen controls the size of material leaving the mill before it moves to the next stage.
A vibrating screen separates rock by size as smaller particles pass through its panels. Larger material moves to the next stage or returns for further crushing.
A slurry pump moves water mixed with solids, such as mill discharge and tailings. Its components need to suit the abrasive material and required flow in your plant.
